title: Theorem 3.4(c): effective degree bound stated but only finiteness proved

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Theorem 3.4(c).

The statement asserts $I$ is generated in degree 'at most a constant depending only on $N$ and $\max_j d_j$.' The proof, however, establishes only finiteness/termination of Buchberger's algorithm and explicitly says 'We do not need the optimal bound, only finiteness.' A bound depending only on $N$ and $\max d_j$ is a substantive effective claim that is not supplied (and is not obviously available at this generality).

**Fix:** either weaken (c) to 'finitely generated', or prove a genuine effective bound — e.g. via Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of $R$ as a graded $k$-algebra, or via Markov/Gröbner degree bounds for the lattice ideal in the diagonal (toric) case.
